newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Spain's king says EU unable to end foreign conflict.
newsitem.headline: Spain's king says EU unable to end foreign conflict.

text.p: Spain's King Juan Carlos said on Monday the European Union's success as an international economic force contrasted with its weakness as a political power, unable to stop tragedy in other parts of the world.

The king was speaking at a ceremony attended by Belgium's King Albert II and Queen Paola at the historic Catholic University of Leuven near Brussels, which awarded him an honorary doctorate for his defence of democracy and humanity.
Police said they had earlier detained 10 students trying to enter the hall to distribute left-wing texts.

"When Yugoslavia fell apart, it was made clear to us in a very cruel way how limited Europe's political influence is outside its own borders, in an area where barbaric practices abound," King Juan Carlos said in an acceptance speech which focused on the past and future development of Europe.
Similarly, he added, neither the EU nor the international community had been able to prevent genocide in Rwanda and the central African region.
"These examples show clearly that the existing mechanisms must be improved by means of tighter collaboration, leading to improved efficiency," he said.

"Europe must not become an island of prosperity and development in the middle of a chaotic world. Our internal stability depends on our capacity to export the results of our development to areas outside the Union."
The king said member states must continue efforts to give a "healthy and convincing start" to the single European currency, planned for 1999.
But governments must also make sure these efforts led to "new and better opportunities for our citizens, without negative consequences for the most vulnerable parts of our population".
